## action

Validate action references, inputs, outputs, and local metadata.

## cache-call-unrestricted

Report reusable workflow calls reachable from low-trust triggers without an explicit cache mode. The called workflow can request cache writes despite the trigger's read-only default.

Set cache-mode to read or none on the calling job or workflow.

- Category: `security/cache`
- Provider: `actionlint`
- Maturity: `stable`
- Enabled by default: `true`

Configure this rule with `lint.rules.security.cache-call-unrestricted`. Use `off` to disable it or `on` to use its default severity. Set `info`, `warn` or `error` to choose a severity. Findings at every enabled level affect the CLI exit status.

## coercion

Warn when a string parameter converts a boolean or null, when a comparison mixes a collection with a type other than null, or when an ordering comparison uses booleans, null or collections. These expressions are valid in GitHub Actions. Unknown types do not establish a suspicious conversion. Collection equality within the same type is allowed because Actions compares instance identity. Equality with null is a presence check and is allowed.

Check the intended argument or operand type. Use a string literal when text is intended, or compare values of the intended types. This rule offers no automatic edit because the intended value is unknown.

- Category: `suspicious/expressions`
- Provider: `actionlint`
- Maturity: `stable`
- Enabled by default: `false`

Configure this rule with `lint.rules.suspicious.coercion`. Use `off` to disable it or `on` to use its default severity. Set `info`, `warn` or `error` to choose a severity. Findings at every enabled level affect the CLI exit status.

Use the boolean value directly when checking branch protection.

```yaml
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: startsWith(github.ref_protected, 'true')
    steps:
      - run: echo ok
```

```yaml
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.ref_protected
    steps:
      - run: echo ok
```

## collection-comparison

Objects and arrays compare equal only when they are the same instance. Equal contents do not make separately created objects or arrays equal. A condition that grants access or gates a write can therefore evaluate differently from a comparison of contents. This check reports == and != between two known objects or two known arrays. It accepts null checks and repeated access to the same context property, and skips unknown types and expressions that cannot execute.

Compare the fields or array elements that determine equality. Disable this rule for a deliberate instance-identity comparison.

- Category: `suspicious/expressions`
- Provider: `actionlint`
- Maturity: `stable`
- Enabled by default: `true`

Configure this rule with `lint.rules.suspicious.collection-comparison`. Use `off` to disable it or `on` to use its default severity. Set `info`, `warn` or `error` to choose a severity. Findings at every enabled level affect the CLI exit status.

Compare the object properties that matter to the condition.

```yaml
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: ${{ fromJSON('{"ready":true}') == fromJSON('{"ready":true}') }}
    steps:
      - run: echo ok
```

```yaml
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: ${{ fromJSON('{"ready":true}').ready == fromJSON('{"ready":true}').ready }}
    steps:
      - run: echo ok
```

## container-runner

GitHub-managed job containers, service containers and Docker actions require Linux and a Docker daemon. Report an error for known Windows or macOS selections. Warn for GitHub-hosted ubuntu-slim: it includes Docker client tools but no local daemon; a compatible remote daemon may satisfy the requirement. Inspect available action metadata and expanded composites, with matrix rows and conditions determining which selections can reach the container. Unknown runner facts and unavailable action bodies do not establish a violation. Docker commands in scripts can use remote daemons and are not classified by this rule.

Select a Linux runner with Docker, such as ubuntu-latest, or guard the container action so incompatible matrix rows do not execute it. For ubuntu-slim, verify any remote daemon configuration before suppressing the warning. Self-hosted Linux runners need an accessible Docker daemon. No automatic fix is offered because changing the runner can change job behavior.

- Category: `correctness/runners`
- Provider: `actionlint`
- Maturity: `stable`
- Enabled by default: `true`

Configure this rule with `lint.rules.correctness.container-runner`. Use `off` to disable it or `on` to use its default severity. Set `info`, `warn` or `error` to choose a severity. Findings at every enabled level affect the CLI exit status.

Use a Linux runner with Docker for a job container.

```yaml
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: windows-latest
    container: alpine:3
    steps:
      - run: echo ok
```

```yaml
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    container: alpine:3
    steps:
      - run: echo ok
```

## errexit-status

With Bash errexit enabled, a failing simple command exits before a following $? read. The read can capture success, but cannot capture the preceding failure.

The check uses registered interpreter options and follows literal set changes, groups, subshells and known branches. This warning is opt-in because a success-only read can be intentional.

The check excludes reads within condition tests, AND/OR lists and pipelines, and reads of compound-command results. It skips trap bodies, function bodies and command substitutions. Unknown option values suspend analysis until a known set change. Operations that may replace builtins or install traps stop further analysis in that scope.

The rule is experimental because function calls, command substitution inheritance and dynamic option effects are not modeled. Bash behavior is specified at https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/html_node/The-Set-Builtin.html; runner defaults are in actions/runner ScriptHandlerHelpers.cs.

Capture the failure status in an if condition or an || handler when the script must continue after failure.

- Category: `suspicious/scripts`
- Provider: `actionlint`
- Maturity: `nursery`
- Enabled by default: `false`

Configure this rule with `lint.rules.suspicious.errexit-status`. Use `off` to disable it or `on` to use its default severity. Set `info`, `warn` or `error` to choose a severity. Findings at every enabled level affect the CLI exit status.

Capture failure explicitly when the script must continue.

```yaml
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - shell: bash
        run: |
          CHANGED="$(git diff --exit-code)"; EXIT_CODE=$?
```

```yaml
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - shell: bash
        run: |
          CHANGED="$(git diff --exit-code)" || EXIT_CODE=$?
```

## invalid-output-file

GITHUB_OUTPUT requires NAME=value records or multiline records enclosed by NAME<<delimiter and a matching delimiter. This check combines literal writes from Bash and sh scripts, then validates the complete file. It handles literal echo and printf commands, command groups, and cat or tee with literal text from a here-document or pipe. It skips the script if it contains dynamic values, unsupported commands, variable assignments or control flow. Commands that could redefine these utilities also cause the script to be skipped.

Write NAME=value for a single-line output. For a multiline output, write NAME<<delimiter, the value, and the matching delimiter.

- Category: `correctness/scripts`
- Provider: `actionlint`
- Maturity: `stable`
- Enabled by default: `true`

Configure this rule with `lint.rules.correctness.invalid-output-file`. Use `off` to disable it or `on` to use its default severity. Set `info`, `warn` or `error` to choose a severity. Findings at every enabled level affect the CLI exit status.

Write the value as a named output.

```yaml
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - shell: bash
        run: echo '{"available":true}' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
```

```yaml
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - shell: bash
        run: echo 'available=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
```

## join-literal

join() accepts a string and returns it unchanged. Context names inside the quotes are literal text and are not evaluated. The separator has no effect on that string. This optional check reports a string literal as the first argument even when the call may be deliberate. Arrays and strings supplied by other expressions are not reported.

If you meant to use literal text, remove the redundant call. To combine expression values, use format() or pass an array to join(). This rule does not offer an automatic edit.

- Category: `suspicious/expressions`
- Provider: `actionlint`
- Maturity: `nursery`
- Enabled by default: `false`

Configure this rule with `lint.rules.suspicious.join-literal`. Use `off` to disable it or `on` to use its default severity. Set `info`, `warn` or `error` to choose a severity. Findings at every enabled level affect the CLI exit status.

## missing-permissions

Report jobs with no permissions declared on the job or workflow. Set require-at to workflow or every-job to require permissions there. An array requires permissions at every listed location. When require-at is omitted, workflows triggered only by workflow_call are skipped. The workflow-call rule compares the caller's permissions with those requested by the called workflow.

Add permissions on the workflow or on every job. If require-at is configured, add permissions at every location it lists. Use permissions: {} to grant none. See [CodeQL's explanation of missing workflow permissions](https://codeql.github.com/codeql-query-help/actions/actions-missing-workflow-permissions/). Set the rule to off to disable it.

- Category: `security/permissions`
- Provider: `actionlint`
- Maturity: `stable`
- Enabled by default: `true`

Configure this rule with `lint.rules.security.missing-permissions`. Use `off` to disable it or `on` to use its default severity. Set `info`, `warn` or `error` to choose a severity. Findings at every enabled level affect the CLI exit status.

This job uses no token permissions.

```yaml
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo ok
```


## mixed-type-comparisons

Flag condition comparisons that implicitly convert scalar types.

## numeric-values

Report numeric values GitHub truncates toward zero or that cannot take effect, such as a fractional or non-positive max-parallel.

Set max-parallel to a positive whole number.

- Category: `correctness/values`
- Provider: `actionlint`
- Maturity: `stable`
- Enabled by default: `true`

Configure this rule with `lint.rules.correctness.numeric-values`. Use `off` to disable it or `on` to use its default severity. Set `info`, `warn` or `error` to choose a severity. Findings at every enabled level affect the CLI exit status.

Write the whole number GitHub uses for max-parallel.

```yaml
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      max-parallel: 1.5
      matrix:
        n: [1, 2]
    steps:
      - run: echo ok
```

```yaml
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      max-parallel: 1
      matrix:
        n: [1, 2]
    steps:
      - run: echo ok
```

## script-injection

Detect untrusted values and secrets interpolated into scripts.

Pass untrusted values through environment variables or action inputs. For secrets, prefer the tool's native environment variable or stdin over command arguments. GitHub secrets are automatically masked; register generated or fetched secrets with add-mask before use. Masking protects logs, not process arguments.

- Category: `security/scripts`
- Provider: `actionlint`
- Maturity: `stable`
- Enabled by default: `true`

Configure this rule with `lint.rules.security.script-injection`. Use `off` to disable it or `on` to use its default severity. Set `info`, `warn` or `error` to choose a severity. Findings at every enabled level affect the CLI exit status.

Prefer the tool's native environment variable: GitHub CLI reads GH_TOKEN directly, keeping the secret out of script text and command arguments. GitHub secrets are automatically masked in logs; register generated or fetched secrets with add-mask before use. Masking does not protect process arguments.

```yaml
# wrong: secret in script text
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.TOKEN }}" gh api user
```

```yaml
# correct: secret in environment variable
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.TOKEN }}
        run: gh api user
```

When supported, pass secrets through stdin. Bash's printf builtin feeds Docker's password-stdin option without putting the password in Docker's arguments. GitHub masks this stored secret automatically; generated or fetched values must be masked before use. Keep shell tracing disabled.

```yaml
# wrong: password in command arguments
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env:
          REGISTRY_USER: ${{ vars.REGISTRY_USER }}
        run: docker login --username "$REGISTRY_USER" --password "${{ secrets.REGISTRY_PASSWORD }}"
```

```yaml
# correct: password through stdin
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - shell: bash
        env:
          REGISTRY_USER: ${{ vars.REGISTRY_USER }}
          REGISTRY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.REGISTRY_PASSWORD }}
        run: printf '%s' "${REGISTRY_PASSWORD}" | docker login --username "${REGISTRY_USER}" --password-stdin
```

## script-interpolation

Detect template values that may change script syntax. Unknown strings are checked independently of attacker control. Constrained, nonempty literal strings can be used as shell words; empty and all-decimal strings need a proved data-argument position. Booleans, numeric values, optional matrix members, numeric identifiers, SHA values, and hashFiles results also require that position.

Pass dynamic values through environment variables and read them as data in the script. Quoting a template expression does not prevent substitution before script parsing.

- Category: `correctness/scripts`
- Provider: `actionlint`
- Maturity: `stable`
- Enabled by default: `true`

Configure this rule with `lint.rules.correctness.script-interpolation`. Use `off` to disable it or `on` to use its default severity. Set `info`, `warn` or `error` to choose a severity. Findings at every enabled level affect the CLI exit status.

Keep a dynamic value out of generated shell source.

```yaml
# wrong: template value in script text
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "${{ vars.MESSAGE }}"
```

```yaml
# better: template value in environment variable
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - env: { MESSAGE: "${{ vars.MESSAGE }}" }
        run: echo "${MESSAGE}"
```

Best when logging untrusted text: keep the environment binding and suspend workflow-command processing around the output. Use a fresh unpredictable token for each invocation, keep shell tracing disabled, and register any secret masks before stopping commands. The EXIT trap resumes commands even if printing fails. This protects the log command channel; it does not sanitize shell source, hide secrets, or escape terminal control characters. If raw text is unnecessary, use a serializer or escaping routine for the intended output format. See [GitHub's stop-commands guidance](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-commands#stopping-and-starting-workflow-commands).

```yaml
# best: untrusted log output cannot issue workflow commands
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - shell: bash
        env: { MESSAGE: "${{ vars.MESSAGE }}" }
        run: |
          stop_token="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
          trap 'printf "::%s::\n" "${stop_token}"' EXIT
          printf '::stop-commands::%s\n' "${stop_token}"
          printf '%s\n' "${MESSAGE}"
```

## uncancellable-condition

Opt-in policy for job conditions using always() that can evaluate to true during cancellation. Cleanup and cancellation notifications can require this behavior; the condition alone does not prove a mistake. Step conditions are not reported because action names do not establish whether their work is needed for cleanup. cancel-timeout-minutes does not force cancellation of a job whose condition keeps it running. Warning when enabled; --strict enables this policy as an error, including intentional uses.

If cancellation should stop the job, use !cancelled(). Keep always() when cancellation cleanup or reporting must run. A standalone always() offers a behavior-changing fix requiring explicit review; compound conditions have no replacement. See [GitHub's always() guidance](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/expressions#always) and the [job-versus-step cancellation test](https://github.com/kjanat/actionlint/actions/runs/41520665123).

- Category: `suspicious/expressions`
- Provider: `actionlint`
- Maturity: `stable`
- Enabled by default: `false`

Configure this rule with `lint.rules.suspicious.uncancellable-condition`. Use `off` to disable it or `on` to use its default severity. Set `info`, `warn` or `error` to choose a severity. Findings at every enabled level affect the CLI exit status.

When this job should stop on cancellation, use !cancelled(). Do not make this change for required cancellation cleanup or reporting.

```yaml
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: ${{ always() }}
    steps:
      - run: echo ok
```

```yaml
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    steps:
      - run: echo ok
```

## unused-suppression

Report each inline suppression selector that matches no enabled findings in the checked YAML declaration. Information by default; errors with --strict. A selector used by any analyzed invocation of the same source is considered used. Incomplete analyses do not establish that a selector is unused.

Run actionlint fix --apply or use the editor quick fix to remove unused selectors. Selectors that suppress findings and the comment's reason are preserved. A suppression comment is removed when all its selectors are unused. Configure lint.rules.correctness.unused-suppression to change its level.

- Category: `correctness/suppressions`
- Provider: `actionlint`
- Maturity: `stable`
- Enabled by default: `true`

Configure this rule with `lint.rules.correctness.unused-suppression`. Use `off` to disable it or `on` to use its default severity. Set `info`, `warn` or `error` to choose a severity. Findings at every enabled level affect the CLI exit status.

## vendor-lock-in

GitHub Actions accepts repository shorthand in uses. It does not accept full repository URLs. On the github execution target, report URL references in action steps and reusable-workflow calls. An HTTPS github.com URL offers a safe fix that removes its prefix while preserving the repository, action path and ref. Other hosts have no automatic substitution: the same owner/repository name on GitHub does not establish the same action. Docker registry URLs, local actions and dynamic references are excluded. Other execution targets are not restricted by this rule.

Use owner/repo[/path]@ref for an action hosted in the current GitHub instance. To use an externally hosted action, choose and verify a GitHub mirror, or check out the external source and invoke its local action. The prefix fix is unavailable for URLs with credentials, ports, URL encoding, queries, fragments or invalid shorthand.

- Category: `correctness/dependencies`
- Provider: `actionlint`
- Maturity: `stable`
- Enabled by default: `true`

Configure this rule with `lint.rules.correctness.vendor-lock-in`. Use `off` to disable it or `on` to use its default severity. Set `info`, `warn` or `error` to choose a severity. Findings at every enabled level affect the CLI exit status.

Remove the GitHub URL prefix without changing the action or its version.

```yaml
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: https://github.com/mlugg/setup-zig@v2
```

```yaml
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: mlugg/setup-zig@v2
```

## workflow-command-syntax

The runner prints malformed or unknown :: commands as ordinary text. They do not create annotations or apply command effects.

This opt-in warning checks literal echo and printf output in Bash or POSIX shells, print calls in Python, and Write-Host, Write-Output or echo calls in PowerShell. It joins writes into stdout lines, including stop and resume tokens split across writes. Command processing is evaluated separately for each possible execution path. Comments and unused strings do not produce findings.

Registered interpreter settings and literal set changes determine errexit. Known failures and exit commands end execution. The check handles the errexit exceptions for conditions, negation and AND/OR lists. Unsupported commands, dynamic output, loops and complex control flow stop analysis of that path. A pending partial line is checked only at a known end of output. Python and PowerShell scripts are skipped entirely when a statement cannot be parsed by the limited literal-output model.

The rule is experimental because language coverage is partial and command-shaped text may be an intentional example. The syntax and case-insensitive extension list follow actions/runner revision 1ba885c2065fd9be317808ab3fd406f392635cf7, ActionCommand.cs and ActionCommandManager.cs. Extension-specific properties are not validated.

Use ::name::message or ::name key=value::message with a runner command name. Use stop-commands when intentionally printing command examples.

- Category: `suspicious/scripts`
- Provider: `actionlint`
- Maturity: `nursery`
- Enabled by default: `false`

Configure this rule with `lint.rules.suspicious.workflow-command-syntax`. Use `off` to disable it or `on` to use its default severity. Set `info`, `warn` or `error` to choose a severity. Findings at every enabled level affect the CLI exit status.

Close the annotation name with two colons.

```yaml
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - shell: bash
        run: echo "::notice:Up to date"
```

```yaml
on: push
permissions: {}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - shell: bash
        run: echo "::notice::Up to date"
```
